spine: Until you learn there is a pocket of air behind each eardrum.
Because of that, the climb lets air out and you hear a pop.
Because of that, landing has to push air back in, and the tube resists.
Until finally a swallow pulls it open and your ears match the sky.

acts.name: The question
acts.beats: Why do your ears pop on a plane?

acts.name: The pocket
acts.beats: A tiny air pocket behind the eardrum, a thin tube to the throat, balanced on the ground.

acts.name: The climb
acts.beats: But the cabin air thins; the trapped air pushes out; so the tube pops open.

acts.name: The landing
acts.beats: But landing is the opposite and harder; so swallow, yawn or chew to pull the tube open.

acts.name: The click
acts.beats: That click is your ears matching the sky. End card: Tiny Whys, follow for part 2.

output.turn: The landing is harder because the tube lets air out easily but lets it in reluctantly; a swallow is what pulls it open.
output.reason: An If/But/So chain built only from the five sourced facts: each beat answers the last and raises the next, with the reversal (landing is worse) at about 55 %.
